title: London System against the King's Indian setup
line: The same plan when Black puts its bishop on the long diagonal.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares. It takes the center and frees your bishop.
steps.after: Black brings a knight out first.

steps.text: Bring the knight out. It guards the center square e5.
steps.after: Black gets ready to put its bishop on the long diagonal: the King's Indian setup.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out before you move the king pawn, as in every London System.
Move the pawn in front of your king one square. It guards your center pawn and frees the other bishop.
Bring the other bishop out so that you can castle.
Push the pawn on h2 one square. If a knight comes to h5, your bishop can step back to h2, out of its reach.

also.e1g1: Castling is sound too. This lesson makes room for the bishop first.

steps.text: Castle. Your king is safe, and the rook can join the game.
Move the pawn on c2 one square. It backs up your center pawn against the pawn on c5.
steps.after: The same triangle of pawns, with the bishop safe from Black's knight.

summary: Against the bishop on the long diagonal, the London setup stays the same, with a pawn push to keep the bishop safe.
